user.title: New safe filter
user.description: Clean up and smooth one sensor, or combine several sensors into one trustworthy value.

single.title: Filter one sensor
single.description: Turn one sensor into a trustworthy, smoothed value. Readings that are unavailable, stale or out of range are ignored, and the last good value is held for a while instead.

combine.title: Combine several sensors
combine.description: Combine several sensors into one trustworthy value. Sources that are unavailable, stale, out of range or disagree with the others are left out automatically.

data_description.entity_ids: Sensors to combine. Drag to reorder: with the Priority method, the first valid sensor is used.
data_description.method: How the valid sources are combined into one value.

weights.title: Weights
weights.description:
Give each source a relative weight. A source with weight 2 counts twice as much as one with weight 1. Weights are renormalised over the sources that are valid at any moment.

{sources}

data_description.min_weight: The valid sources must together carry at least this share of the total weight to compute a new value. With weights 5, 3 and 2 and 50 %, the first source alone or the other two together are enough, but the last one alone is not. Applies in addition to Minimum valid sources. 0 turns it off.
data_description.offset_learning: While all sources are valid, learn how far each one usually is from the combined value, and correct for it when one drops out, so the value doesn't jump. This sets how quickly the learned offsets follow changes; 60 min is a good start. 0 turns it off.

quality.title: Data quality
quality.description: Rules that decide whether a source can be trusted. Values are in {unit}.

data.max_deviation: Max deviation from the other sources

data_description.min_value: Readings below this are ignored. Leave empty for no limit.
data_description.max_value: Readings above this are ignored. Leave empty for no limit.
data_description.stale_after: A source that has not reported for this long is ignored. Only turn this on if the source sends its value regularly even when it doesn't change. Many integrations, such as ESPHome and MQTT, only send changes, so a steady value would be treated as a dead device. 0 turns the check off.
data_description.max_deviation: With 3 or more valid sources, a source further than this from the median of all of them is ignored. Leave empty to turn off.
data_description.min_sources: How many sources must be valid to compute a new value.
data_description.hold_time: When there is no valid reading (or too few valid sources), keep showing the last good value this long, then become unavailable. Also covers restarts.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: Optional filters, applied in this order to the source value (or the combined value). Values are in {unit}. Each smoother (3 to 5) adds delay, so usually one of them is enough. Each chart shows one filter on its own, applied to the same noisy example: grey is the input, blue the output.

data_description.precision: Rounding is applied to the final value only.

data_description.window_size: Number of recent samples to compare against.
data_description.radius:
A sample further than this from the median of the window is ignored. A real, lasting change is accepted after about half the window. Red rings mark ignored samples.

![Spike rejection on a noisy example]({outlier_chart})

data_description.max_rate:
The value may not change faster than this, in the sensor's unit per minute.

![Rate limit on a noisy example]({rate_limit_chart})

data_description.time_constant:
Exponential smoothing on real time, also known as a low-pass filter. After one time constant the output has moved about 63% of the way to a new level, no matter how often the sources report. Between reports, and while the last value is held, it keeps moving toward the last valid reading.

![Low-pass on a noisy example]({lowpass_chart})

data_description.readings:
Each new valid reading moves the output 2/(N+1) of the way toward it: with 5 readings, a third of the way. A source that sends the same value again counts each time. Time plays no part: if the source stops reporting, the output stays where it is, so for sources that only send changes the average over time is usually better.

![Exponential moving average over readings on a noisy example]({ema_chart})

data_description.window:
Time-weighted average over this period.

![Moving average on a noisy example]({moving_average_chart})

error.no_sources: Select at least one source sensor.
error.duplicate_sources: The same sensor is selected more than once.
error.incompatible_units: The selected sensors have units that cannot be converted to each other.
error.min_not_below_max: The lowest plausible value must be lower than the highest.
error.min_sources_too_high: Minimum valid sources can't be higher than the number of selected sensors.
error.max_rate_not_positive: Max change per minute must be greater than 0.
